title: Funding bid for Kitchener recreation complex quad gym
subtitle: Also approved: Oktoberfest noise exemption and youth climate grant agreements, both adopted through a finance committee report.
overview: Council voted to back grant applications to the provincial Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund and the federal Green and Inclusive Community Buildings program. The money would pay for a four-court gymnasium attached to the Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex at RBJ Schlegel Park. The total gym budget is set at $29,913,529 {{vote:m4}}.

If both grants are awarded, up to $9,913,529 in debt financing is authorized. If only one is awarded, the limit is $19,913,529. Either way the term is no more than 20 years, repaid from development charge revenue set aside for indoor recreation. Staff said this means no property tax impact. Staff said building the gym alongside the current project would cost less and open it sooner, in summer 2026. Council also directed staff to report back if grant funding is not secured, so Council can decide how to proceed.

Council also adopted a finance committee report {{vote:m1}}. It included a noise exemption for K-W Oktoberfest events from September 27 to October 19 {{vote:m2}} and authority to sign agreements with Youth Climate Action Fund grant recipients {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.detail: Council supported applying to the provincial and federal grant programs for the quad gymnasium and set its total budget at $29,913,529, as amended {{vote:m4}}.
Council authorized up to $9,913,529 in debt if both grants succeed, or up to $19,913,529 if only one does, over no more than 20 years and repaid from development charges.
Staff must report to Council with options if the grant funding is unsuccessful, or by information report on the application status if it succeeds.
K-W Oktoberfest Inc. received an exemption from the Noise by-law for events at various clubs from September 27 to October 19, 2024.
The CAO and General Managers were authorized to sign agreements with Youth Climate Action Fund grant recipients, to the City Solicitor's satisfaction.

debate: Staff said the gym was left out of the original build because it was unaffordable. They said that building it now would cost about 30% less than waiting, and that waiting could mean five or more years before a later build.

Councillors asked how reliable the provincial and federal funding is. Staff said they could not predict grant outcomes but felt the project fit the criteria well. They said applying early and moving quickly lowers the risk of funding being withdrawn.
On property taxes, staff said the project would be funded from development charges, so no tax impact is expected. The grants mainly help with cash flow.
Councillors in support pointed to demand for pickleball, basketball, volleyball and badminton space, and to the chance of drawing tournaments and tourism.

One councillor opposed the clause requiring a report back if funding fails. They called it a slow way of backing out and said the City should avoid building infrastructure it cannot afford. That clause was voted on separately and carried, and the rest of the motion carried.
